citation: Llosa, L., Lee, O., Jiang, F., Haas, A., O'Connor, C., Van Booven, C. D., & Kieffer, M. J. (2016). Impact of a large-scale science intervention focused on English language learners. American Educational Research Journal, 53(2), 395-424. https://doi.org/10.3102/0002831216637348
report_number: American Educational Research Journal, 53(2), 395-424; DOI 10.3102/0002831216637348; NSF Grant DRL 1209309 (P-SELL: Promoting Science among English Language Learners)
design: Cluster (school-level) RCT; 66 elementary schools (33 treatment / 33 control) randomized within 3 districts in one Southeastern state; Grade 5 science; treatment = P-SELL year-long science curriculum + 5 full-day teacher professional-development workshops vs business-as-usual (district-adopted textbooks); ~6,239 students with outcome data (analysis student n=5,752 researcher-developed, 6,173 state assessment), 2012-13 (Year 1 of a 3-year implementation). Outcomes = researcher-developed science assessment (NAEP/TIMSS/state release items, pre+post, max 31 pts) and high-stakes state science assessment (60-66 MC items, scale 140-260).
problems: The paper reports HLM treatment coefficients (b) and standardized effect sizes (d) but does NOT report standard errors of the treatment coefficient (Tables 5-7 give only significance stars). The reported d is the pretest-adjusted (3-level HLM) impact coefficient divided by the pooled posttest SD: I confirmed this exactly -- researcher-developed b=1.41/pooled SD 5.656=0.249 (reported 0.25); state b=3.28/pooled SD 22.11=0.148 (reported 0.15). g=J*d with J~=1.0000 at these N, so g equals the reported d to displayed precision. Because the model SE is not reported, g_var/g_se were computed from the standard student-level large-sample variance formula and therefore do NOT account for clustering: cluster_adjusted=false. n_clusters (66) and the school-level design-effect ICC (derived from the Table 5/6/7 variance components: school/(school+teacher+student)) are recorded per effect so the variance can be cluster-corrected centrally (Hedges 2007). n_t/n_c per effect are the Table 4 group descriptive sample sizes (analysis used multiply-imputed pretest with slightly different total Ns shown in Tables 5-7). The four language-proficiency subgroup contrasts (Tables 6-7) are non-randomised subsets (outcome_role=subgroup, is_full_sample=false). Only the two full-sample science outcomes are primary. All outcomes are science => STEM.

effect_sizes.test_name: Researcher-developed science assessment (NAEP/TIMSS/state release items; pre+post; max 31 pts)
effect_sizes.g_method: HLM (3-level) pretest-adjusted treatment coefficient b=1.41 standardized by pooled posttest SD (5.656) => d=0.249; authors report d=0.25. g=J*d, J=0.99987 (df=N-2, N=5752) => g=0.25. Var(d) from student-level formula (N+n)/(n_t*n_c)+d^2/(2N) with n_t=2894,n_c=3345; Var(g)=J^2*Var(d). NOT cluster-adjusted (model SE not reported).

effect_sizes.notes: Full-sample headline outcome, RQ1. d=0.25, p<.001 (Benjamini-Hochberg corrected). Analysis student n=5,752; teacher n=252; school n=66. School-level ICC=0.0087, school+teacher ICC=0.096 (from Table 5 variance components school=0.13, teacher=1.31, student=13.52).
